claims.scope: operating-performance exposure to customer cloud/data workload usage and technology-spending optimization
claims.temporal_basis: The hypothesis combines operating-model disclosures in two separate annual filings; each source has its own reporting period and neither describes a relationship interval.
claims.interpretation: Both companies' disclosures support a testable hypothesis that customer workload and technology-spending changes can affect operating performance: Datadog says customer usage expands with cloud workloads and warns that IT spending changes may affect its business; Snowflake reports consumption-based product revenue and says customers may optimize consumption in response to macroeconomic uncertainty. This establishes a common possible driver, not shared customers or observed co-movement.

sources.publisher: Datadog, Inc. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.evidence_locator: Form 10-K, Item 7, Overview and Revenue; printed pages 44 and 47
sources.evidence_text: Datadog says customers expand usage as they expand public- and private-cloud workloads, describes host- and data-volume-based usage pricing, and warns that businesses may slow IT spending during economic uncertainty.
sources.evidence_quote: We grow with our customers as they expand their workloads

sources.publisher: Snowflake Inc. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.evidence_locator: Form 10-K, Item 7, revenue model and customer consumption/macroeconomic risk discussion
sources.evidence_text: Snowflake says most revenue comes from customer consumption of compute, storage, and data transfer, and warns that customers may rationalize budgets and optimize consumption amid macroeconomic uncertainty.
sources.evidence_quote: customers may continue to optimize consumption, rationalize budgets

claims.alternative_or_unknown: Revenue sensitivity may differ because Datadog's revenue is largely subscription-based while Snowflake recognizes most product revenue on consumption. No shared-customer evidence has been established. Revenue and stock-return co-movement remain untested, as do causal effects and effect size.
